problem: A teacher gives you a test with a set of fifteen questions, out of which you are told to answer ten. How many ways can you answer ten different questions?
worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $15$ questions, so $n=15.$ We want to select $10$ of those questions to answer, so we have $r=10.$

Therefore, the number of ways to answer $10$ different questions is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{15}{C}_{10} & =\frac{15!}{(15-10)!\,10!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{5!10!} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12\cdot 11\cdot \cancel{10!}}{5!\cancel{10!}} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot 13\cdot 12\cdot 11}{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{360\,360}{120} \\  & =3\,003.\end{aligned}
$$
